newsitem.title: USA: U.S. moves to limit fishing of Atlantic swordfish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. moves to limit fishing of Atlantic swordfish.

text.p: The National Marine Fisheries Service Monday proposed measures to try to rebuild Atlantic swordfish stocks by limiting access to the fishery.

With swordfish stocks estimated at 67 percent of optimum levels and the average size of landed fish at 84 pounds compared to 266 pounds 30 years ago, the agency said commercial harvesting capacity must be limited.
"Historically, the swordfish fishery has operated under open access, but that can't continue any longer," Rolland Schmitten, fisheries service director, said in a statement.
The agency said far more permits are issued for swordfish than are actually used and said this excessive harvesting capacity should be reduced.
Proposed new management practice would base access to the fishery on past levels of participation, restrict transfer of permits, and establish vessel upgrading restrictions and ownership limits.

The agency also proposed having two kinds of commercial permits, with one for owners of vessels that use nets that may catch other fish and a less restrictive permit for vessels that use handgear including rod-and-reel and harpoons.
All landed swordfish would have to be reported to the fisheries service to help determine the status of the stocks and to enforce fishing quotas.
